To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the voltage-induced pores are Ca2+ channels, and that the Ca2+ influx triggers localized cortical granule exocytosis.

a high-voltage pulse of 1 kilo-volt per centimeter for 100 microseconds causes the entrance of calcium into sea urchin eggs, that calcium is required to trigger cortical granules to break, and that the calcium-induced cortical granule breakdown causes the formation of a partial fertilizaton envelope.

(1) a single voltage pulse of 100 microseconds duration at 1 kV/ cm in sea-urchins eggs induces localized exocytotic breakdown of cortical granules; (2) the breakdown is triggered by Ca2+ entry through voltage-induced pores; (3) the breakdown occurs at the loci where the anode faces; and (4) the breakdown is not accompanied by the wave spreading of the partial fertilization envelope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of Ca in the early events in fertilization of sea urchin eggs.
the role of Ca(2+) in the events that follow fertilization of sea urchin eggs.
the use of high voltage pulses to produce pores and the use of these pores to investigate the mechanism of Ca2+ uptake and its role in fertilization of sea urchin eggs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ is the trigger for cortical granule exocytosis and the formation of the fertilisation envelope.
the voltage pulsation method provides a useful tool in the study of the role of Ca(2+) in the fertilization process.
the voltage pulsation technique can be used to investigate the early events in fertilization in the absence of sperm and to determine the role of Ca+2 in these processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voltage-induced pores provide a convenient means for studying the early events of fertilization.
the fertilization envelope is not a single-cell membrane.
Ca2+ is the primary trigger for the events in the first 30 minutes of fertilization in sea urchin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that it is possible to trigger a specific event (in this case cortical granule breakdown) in the cell cycle of an egg by the use of a voltage pulse.
voltage pulsation is a powerful technique for studying the role of Ca in cell activation.
the voltage pulse technique can be used as a tool to induce localized, Ca2+-dependent events in cells.
